notes: Summary: enterprise logistics platform evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency chat + reranking across US/CA regions.
POC complete 2/16: 24h steady-state test + 3 burst windows. Measured sustained 120k tokens/sec across 8x80GB A100-equivalent with batching. Target: contractual min 100k tokens/sec per pod.
Key ask from procurement: guaranteed min tokens/sec (contract), concurrency caps per tenant, and a documented burst policy (duration, throttle behavior, cost).
Technical: prefer model variants quantized to int8 for cost, but want p95 <= 120ms for short chat; p99 <= 450ms for 2k-token responses under reserved capacity.
We proposed reserved pool: 8 GPUs pinned (primary), 2-GPU burst pool (paid), and fallback to hosted API with model fallback (smaller model) when reserved exhausted.
SE notes (Diego): measured tail latency improvement with prefix caching and KV reuse between sessions; autoscaling cooldown set to 10m to avoid flapping during delivery windows.
Customer quote during workshop: 'We need predictable throughput during morning dispatch spikes — if you underdeliver, our SLAs to freight partners break.'
Procurement asks: service credits formula linked to tokens/sec shortfall and p99 breaches; minimum 90% availability of reserved pool during business hours (06:00-22:00 PT).
Security: must support SSO (SAML), KMS integration for secrets, audit logs exported to customer SIEM; retention controls for PII to 30 days.
Commercial sensitivity: price per reserved GPU + separate burst usage rate; customer prefers a blended monthly ARR quote to fit capex vs opex split.

Open questions: 1) How is 'tokens/sec' defined (user tokens vs model tokens) in the SLA? 2) How are multi-tenant concurrency caps enforced on a shared instance? 3) What happens to in-flight requests when fallback to hosted occurs?
Action items from 2/18 meeting: SE to produce formal throughput SLA language, Pricing to produce burst pool price table, Legal to propose service credit thresholds.
use_case_summary: Primary workload: multi-tenant conversational assistants for dispatch + reranking of candidate delivery routes. Requires deterministic throughput during peak windows (07:00-10:30 PT and 16:00-19:00 PT). Latency SLOs needed for both chat and short-form reranking; heavy cost sensitivity on sustained per-token costs.
throughput_requirements: Contractual target: min 100k tokens/sec (sustained over 10-minute windows) across reserved pool
Peak concurrency target: support 1,200 concurrent active sessions with average request sizes 80-200 tokens
Burst policy: allow bursts up to additional 40k tokens/sec for up to 15 minutes (pay-as-you-go burst pool) with automated throttling beyond that
Failover: automatic fallback to Redwood hosted API with tiered model variant (smaller) after 2-minute grace if burst pool exhausted
SLO latency targets: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 150ms, p99 < 450ms for <=512 token responses on reserved capacity
infrastructure_plan: Reserved hardware: 8x 80GB-class GPUs (customer will commit monthly capacity)
Burst pool: shared 2x-GPU burst enclave with per-minute metering
Network: VPC peering + private link, customer-managed firewall rules
Redundancy: active/passive region failover to secondary VPC region (same cloud provider) with warm standby model replicas
Monitoring: token-level cost breakdown, p99 trace retention 90 days; alerts for sustained tokens/sec < contractual min
sla_negotiation_points: Definition of 'tokens/sec' for SLA accounting (model-emitted tokens vs user-supplied tokens)
Measurement windows and smoothing (10-minute vs 1-hour averaging)
Service credit tiers tied to % shortfall from min tokens/sec and p99 latency breaches
Concurrency caps per account and allowed overage behavior
Burst pricing and automatic throttling thresholds
Termination rights if Reserved pool availability < 85% over a billing month
poc_results_summary: POC (2/14-2/16) simulated morning ramp with synthetic traffic and real prompt mixes. Sustained 24h throughput average 115k tokens/sec; two 10-minute bursts hit 150k tokens/sec using temporary QoS settings. Observed p99 spikes during cold-starts for large context window (4k tokens) — mitigations: pre-warm + KV cache reuse.
commercial_notes: Customer prefers 36-month reserved agreement with a 12-month runway for capacity scaling. Wants blended monthly charge with separate line-item for burst usage. Finance requests clause to convert up to 20% of committed capacity to credits if underutilized.
legal_notes: Customer counsel pushing back on penalty ladder; proposing cap at 6 months of fees. Need to align on definition of outage vs degraded performance. Data residency clause required for Canadian customers (logistics stations).
